snp1.6:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.
snp1.6:1.3: Then a certain god, towards the end of the night, whose surpassing beauty lit up the whole of Jeta’s Wood, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he stood on one side.
snp1.6:1.4: While standing on one side that god recited a verse to the Fortunate One:
snp1.6:2.1: “We ask (reverend) Gotama regarding the man going to ruin -
snp1.6:2.3: we have come to ask the Fortunate One,
snp1.6:2.4: what is the cause of ruination?”
snp1.6:3.1: “The thriving man is easy to know,
snp1.6:3.2: the ruining man is easy to know,
snp1.6:3.3: the thriving man loves the Dhamma,
snp1.6:3.4: the ruining man hates the Dhamma.”
snp1.6:4.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know,
snp1.6:4.2: this is the first ruin (of man).
snp1.6:4.3: Please tell us, Fortunate One, what is the second cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:5.2: he does not endear the good,
snp1.6:5.3: he is pleased with the Dhamma of the bad,
snp1.6:5.4: that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:6.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know, this is the second ruin (of man).
snp1.6:6.3: Please tell us, Fortunate One, what is the third cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:7.1: “That man who is fond of sleep,
snp1.6:7.3: lazy, and marked by anger, that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:8.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know, this is the third ruin (of man).
snp1.6:8.3: Please tell us, Fortunate One, what is the fourth cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:9.1: “He who, when his mother or father has grown old, with their youth gone,
snp1.6:9.3: though having much, does not support them, that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:10.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know, this is the fourth ruin (of man).
snp1.6:10.3: Please tell us, Fortunate One, what is the fifth cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:11.2: or an ascetic, or another mendicant
snp1.6:11.3: with words that are false, that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:12.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know, this is the fifth ruin (of man).
snp1.6:12.3: Please tell us, Fortunate One, what is the sixth cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:13.2: who has gold, who has food,
snp1.6:13.3: but who eats his sweetmeats alone, that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:14.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know, this is the sixth ruin (of man).
snp1.6:14.3: Please tell us, Fortunate One, what is the seventh cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:15.1: “That man who is proud of his birth,
snp1.6:15.3: and who despises his kinsfolk, that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:16.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know, this is the seventh ruin (of man).
snp1.6:16.3: Please tell us, Fortunate One, what is the eighth cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:17.1: “That man who is a womanizer, a drunkard, and a gambler,
snp1.6:17.3: who destroys whatever is gained, that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:18.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know, this is the eighth ruin (of man).
snp1.6:18.3: Please tell us, Fortunate One, what is the ninth cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:19.1: “(He who is) not satisfied with his own wives,
snp1.6:19.3: and is seen with other mens’ wives, that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:20.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know, this is the ninth ruin (of man).
snp1.6:20.3: Please tell us, Fortunate One, what is the tenth cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:21.1: “A man who, being past his youth,
snp1.6:21.2: brings home a young girl (for his wife),
snp1.6:21.3: and cannot sleep through jealousy, that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:22.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know, this is the tenth ruin (of man).
snp1.6:22.3: Please tell us, Fortunate One, what is the eleventh cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:23.1: “A woman given to drink, a spendthrift,
snp1.6:23.2: or a man of similar sort,
snp1.6:23.3: appointing (such a one) as overlord, that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:24.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know, this is the eleventh ruin (of man).
snp1.6:24.3: Please tell us, Fortunate One, what is the twelfth cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:25.1: “One who is poor, but has great craving,
snp1.6:25.2: who is born in a family of nobles,
snp1.6:25.3: and who wants to be king, that is a cause of ruination.
snp1.6:26.1: The wise man who reflects on (the cause of) these ruins in the world,
snp1.6:26.3: a noble one, endowed with insight,
